plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a dual-band quarter-wave optical thickness (QWOT) seeded initialization improves convergence for a dichroic HfO2/SiO2 stack compared to uniform-perturbation starts. The prior knowledge is that quarter-wave stacks create constructive interference at design wavelengths, and seeding near lambda/4n for both target bands (500 nm for UV-blue reflection, 1400 nm for SWIR transmission) should give the optimizer a physically meaningful starting point. This route uses no retrieved literature; all justification is from recalled thin-film design principles.

routes.title: Dual-band QWOT-seeded 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses near quarter-wave optical thickness for both the reflection band center (~375 nm) and transmission band center (~1350 nm) will produce higher target scores and faster convergence than uniform-random initialization for the same 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 topology.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks produce maximum reflectance when each layer has optical thickness lambda/4 at the design wavelength. For a dichroic filter, seeding thicknesses that simultaneously approximate lambda_reflect/4n for the high-index layers and lambda_transmit/4n for the low-index layers should create constructive interference in the reflection band while maintaining transmission in the SWIR band. This is recalled from standard thin-film interference theory.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (24 coating layers, alternating HfO2/SiO2 starting with HfO2)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers, initialized from dual-band QWOT calculation and optimized within [20, 200] nm bounds
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
maintain physical validity (no negative thickness, no absorption violations)
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count fixed at 24 (within 30-layer limit)
all thicknesses constrained to [20, 200] nm for manufacturability
alternating material order fixed to simplify deposition sequencing
theory_basis: Quarter-wave optical thickness (lambda/4n) produces maximum reflectance for a given material pair at the design wavelength, recalled from thin-film interference theory
Dichroic filters can be designed by balancing optical thicknesses for multiple wavelength bands, recalled from standard coating design practice
HfO2 has higher refractive index than SiO2 in the visible and SWIR, making it the high-index material in this pair, recalled from material property knowledge
Starting optimization near a physically meaningful point (QWOT) typically converges faster than random initialization, recalled from numerical optimization practice
expected_advantages: QWOT seeding should reduce the number of optimization iterations needed to reach high target scores
Dual-band seeding may find better local optima than single-band or uniform-random starts
Fixed 24-layer alternating topology keeps the search space bounded and interpretable
known_risks: The exact refractive index values of hfo2 and sio2 at 375 nm and 1350 nm are recalled approximately; the local registry will provide measured data
I am uncertain whether 24 layers is optimal versus 20 or 28 layers for this specific band combination; this route does not explore layer count
The QWOT calculation assumes normal incidence; if the actual camera operates at oblique angles, the optimal thicknesses would shift
I recall HfO2 extinction coefficient is low in SWIR but cannot guarantee it without checking the dataset; high absorption would degrade transmission
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer dielectric coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Materials alternate HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) starting with HfO2 as layer 1. Optimize all 24 layer thicknesses within bounds [20, 200] nm. Initialize thicknesses using dual-band quarter-wave optical thickness: for HfO2 layers use t ≈ 375 nm / (4 * n_HfO2_at_375nm) and for SiO2 (Lemarchand) layers use t ≈ 1350 nm / (4 * n_SiO2 (Lemarchand)_at_1350nm), then apply gradient-based optimization with mutation step-size reduced by 50% compared to uniform-perturbation baseline. Score candidates by mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm plus mean reflectance in 300-450 nm with equal weighting. Use coherent transfer-matrix method at normal incidence for unpolarized light.
routes.revision_reason: Refinement based on iteration_04 results: replacing uniform-perturbation initialization with dual-band QWOT seeded population as directed by feedback, reducing mutation step-size by 50% to stabilize coarse interference alignment before fine-tuning

unresolved_decisions: Whether 24 layers is the optimal count for this band combination versus 20, 22, 26, or 28 layers
The exact refractive index values of hfo2 and sio2 at 375 nm and 1350 nm from the local registry
Whether the camera operates at exactly normal incidence or has a range of angles that should be averaged
The actual extinction coefficient of hfo2 in the SWIR band from measured data
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If all routes in this study fail to produce physically valid candidates with target_score above 0.5, the problem may require relaxing the 30-layer limit, allowing additional materials, or accepting lower performance in one band.

expected_observations: best_target_score should rise across rounds as QWOT seeding provides better initial candidates than uniform-random
tightest_margin should remain stable or improve as QWOT-initialized designs are physically meaningful
valid_candidates count should be comparable to prior iteration (around 9) since topology and bounds are unchanged
thicknesses_nm should cluster near QWOT values for early candidates then diverge as optimization refines for dual-band performance
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 5 for two consecutive rounds, reduce thickness lower bound from 20 nm to 15 nm and continue
if tightest_margin falls below 0.8 for three consecutive rounds, reduce mutation step-size by another 25% and continue

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
